PUTTING THE “POP” IN POPCORN
Popcorn is a special hard variety of dried corn that pops open and puffs when it is
heated. The kernel has enough internal moisture to become steam, and the kernel
explodes because the steam has nowhere to go.  Different types of popcorn can be
different colors.  Once popped, though, they’re all white or yellow.
Popcorn is an excellent snack food.  It is high in complex carbohydrates, a
source of some fiber, and, depending on how it is
served, low in fat and calories.  When pur-
chasing microwave popcorn, check
labels for saturated fat content.
Try to buy reduced-fat or “lite”
varieties.  Try popping your
own and seasoning it with a
pinch of salt instead of
adding unnecessary fat and
calories by drizzling butter over
the popcorn.  Alternative season-
ings include onion or garlic powders 
or reduced-fat grated cheese.
